metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 5 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'vector search' operator framing / AC1 semantic-stratum justification with the constraint 'Retrieval as shipped is lexical' — state explicitly that the chosen architecture is lexical BM25F over LLM-generated summaries (not raw-text lexical, not embeddings) and that this is what the semantic-stratum benchmark endorses.
evidence: Operator framing: 'This is a vector search problem over summaries of large tickets. A lexical-only local index is insufficient, and provably so'
Constraint: 'Retrieval as shipped is lexical and needs no model credential at all.'
AC1: 'The architecture is justified from the semantic stratum; the lexical stratum is a control'
Measured fact: 'digest-BM25F got 8 of 8 heavy paraphrases at rank 1' and 'a semantic method needs summarization before embedding'
findings.finding: The operator framing and AC1 describe the solution as 'a vector search problem over summaries' justified 'from the semantic stratum', while the constraints section states 'Retrieval as shipped is lexical and needs no model credential at all.' The plan does not reconcile whether the shipped retrieval is embedding/vector-based or lexical (BM25F over LLM digests).
findings.location: Operator framing / Constraints ('The on-demand LLM judge...'/'Discharged') vs AC1
scenarios: An implementer reading AC1 builds/validates an embedding+vector store; another reading the constraints ships lexical BM25F-over-digests and claims done.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Constraints or AC1 clarifying: the shipped retrieval is BM25F over LLM-produced digests — a summarization-based ('semantic') method whose index is lexical, which is why no embedding model credential is needed at retrieval time despite the 'vector search' framing being the original problem statement.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the index path across c670 (ADR text), 4e89, and a350 to one location (ADR 0122 uses `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`), replacing c670's `<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite`.
evidence: c670 Approach: 'the index location (`<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite`, keyed by tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version, rebuilt on mismatch)'
a350 Approach: 'The sibling story builds a lexical FTS5 index under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`, caught up in the read phase.'
4e89 decomposition: 'the FTS5 index, the persisted ticket-dir to dir-hash map, enumeration-based catch-up'
findings.finding: c670 and its sibling children describe the SAME shared derived index at two different filesystem locations. c670's approach records the index path as `<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite`, while a350 states the index lives under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/` and 4e89's decomposition builds the index that a350 reuses. The as-shipped ADR 0122 (produced by c670, binding per parent AC1) records `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`.
scenarios: A reader of the ADR (per AC1 'Checked by reading the ADR') finds an index path that contradicts where 4e89 builds and a350 reuses the index, making the ADR non-reproducing against the sibling implementations.
Two children writing/reading the one shared index at different paths would each build a distinct index, defeating 'reuse the index; add no second retrieval path.'
findings.suggested_fix: Change c670's recorded index path to `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/` to match ADR 0122, 4e89, and a350.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the freshness-key and catch-up description in c670 with a350/4e89/ADR 0122 (per-ticket dir-hash map, enumeration/dir-hash-diff catch-up), dropping the HEAD-SHA-plus-format-version + `git diff --name-only` framing.
evidence: c670 Approach: 'keyed by tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version, rebuilt on mismatch', 'catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update from `git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>`)'
a350 Approach: '...caught up in the read phase'; 4e89 decomposition: 'persisted ticket-dir to dir-hash map, enumeration-based catch-up'

docs/adr/0122:192 'Freshness key. Per ticket, reducer._cache.compute_dir_hash(...)'; :198 'Catch-up rule. Each run diffs the index's recorded dir hashes against the live store'; a repo search for 'format version' in ADR 0122 returns no matches
findings.finding: c670 and its siblings describe the shared index's freshness key and catch-up rule incompatibly. c670 records freshness = tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version (full rebuild on mismatch) and catch-up = `git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>`, whereas a350 and 4e89 describe a per-ticket dir-hash map with enumeration-based read-phase catch-up. The as-shipped ADR 0122 records only the per-ticket `compute_dir_hash` freshness key and a dir-hash-diff catch-up, with no HEAD-SHA and no format version.
findings.location: child c670-c285-a0f9-4b40 (Approach / ADR freshness-key and catch-up clauses)
scenarios: AC1/c670 AC3 require the ADR be read against measure.py output; the ADR's actual per-ticket dir-hash freshness model contradicts c670's plan text describing a HEAD-SHA + format-version model, so the plan and its own deliverable disagree.
4e89 builds a dir-hash map and a350 relies on read-phase per-ticket catch-up; a HEAD-SHA/git-diff model from c670 would not satisfy the zero-dirs-hashed warm assertion (4e89 AC3) the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite c670's freshness-key/catch-up clause to record the per-ticket `compute_dir_hash` key and dir-hash-diff catch-up that ADR 0122 actually documents and that 4e89 implements and a350 reuses.
